sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205], but the path was a step change, not a smooth climb.
Revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021 [D183][D230], then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores, with the pandemic shifting channel and category mix [P51][P55].
The FY2022 collapse in operating income, down 57.0% [D279], followed discretionary category sales declines and markdowns taken to clear excess inventory [P38].
The window reads as a pandemic pull-forward followed by three years of give-back, leaving revenue below its FY2022 peak [F7][F10].
Food & beverage grew from 19.6% of revenue in FY2017 to 23.0% in FY2025 [D484][D506], contributing 0.3pp in FY2025 [D508].
Apparel & accessories fell 4.7% in FY2025, a 0.7pp drag [D564][D565], and home furnishings & décor declined to $15.6 billion from $20.3 billion in FY2021 [S33][S29].
FY2025 comparable sales fell 2.6% on a 2.2% traffic decline and a 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Operating income fell 8.1% in FY2025 against a 1.7% revenue decline [D417][D416], so there was no operating leverage.
Diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% versus net income at 3.4% [F210][F208], as diluted shares fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [X107][X116].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025 [F34], below the 5.6% window median [D590] and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high [D589].
The FY2025 margin slipped 0.3pp [D429], with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D440][D441].
Gross margin fell to 27.9% from 28.2% [P12], and the SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because of a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit [P11].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 4.9pp [D290] as cost of revenue took 4.6pp [D301] on markdowns and elevated inventory costs [P38].
Net margin of 3.5% [F54] sits 1.4pp under operating margin [F34], with the 22.3% tax rate [D403] and $445 million interest expense [X66] the main gaps.
Operating cash flow of $6.6 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025 [F84][D404], and free cash flow of $2.8 billion was 0.77x [F104][D405], under the 1.01x window median [D599].
The FY2025 operating cash decline reflected lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [P7].
Free cash flow margin was 2.7% [D401], below the 4.5% median [D596] and the 4.2% peer median [D611].
Capex of $3.7 billion was 3.6% of revenue and 1.19x D&A [F94][D400][D406], up 28.9% on new stores and remodels [D423][P5].
Net debt was $4.3 billion, or 4.1% of revenue [D410][D411], against a peer median net cash of -3.5% of revenue (n=6) [D613].
Cash and investments rose to $10.1 billion [D408] while total debt reached $14.4 billion [D409], and the current ratio held at 0.94x [F184].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.5 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow [D412][D413], and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D434].
Payout above free cash flow in most years has been funded from the cash pile rather than new leverage, which keeps the balance sheet adequate but not strong.
Revenue has declined three straight years, FY2023 through FY2025 [F8][F9][F10][R1], the most persistent issue in the pack.
The FY2025 drop traces to a 2.6% comparable sales decline on lower traffic [P14], so the trend is demand-led, not store-count-led.
The current ratio of 0.94x [F184][R2] is at the window median [D602], so it reflects normal retail working-capital structure rather than distress.
The 2.4 years of burn coverage [D276][R3] dates from FY2022 and no longer applies, since free cash flow has been positive since [F102][F103][F104].
FY2022 buybacks and FY2017 SG&A were later restated [R5][R6], so those two figures carry a data-quality caveat.
Whether operating margin holds above the 4.9% FY2025 level [F34] or falls toward the 3.5% FY2022 low [D588], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 4.5% median [D596] from 2.7% [D401], given guided FY2026 capex of about $5 billion [P4].
Whether revenue stops declining after three down years [F8][F9][F10], with comparable sales the line to watch in the FY2026 filing [P14].
